# msrest_update_resource (Resource)

Manages a subset of the properties of an existing object behind a REST API that is read with `GET` and written with `PATCH`, `PUT` or `POST`, typically a settings object that always exists. It works like `msgraph_update_resource` of the msgraph provider, for APIs other than Microsoft Graph.

Only the properties in `body` are managed. On every refresh the provider reads the object and compares just those properties, so a change made outside of Terraform shows up as a diff on `body`. Destroying the resource only removes it from the state, unless `delete_method` is set.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Planner tenant settings (singleton). Needs the app role
# OrgSettings-Planner.ReadWrite.All on ProjectWorkManagement. The token scope
# defaults to https://tasks.office.com/.default (the host of url).
resource "msrest_update_resource" "planner" {
  url     = "https://tasks.office.com/taskAPI/tenantAdminSettings/Settings"
  headers = { "OData-Version" = "4.0;NetFx" }
  body = {
    allowCalendarSharing = false
  }
}

# Self-service purchase policy, one object per product. Needs the app role
# Policy.ReadWrite.AllowSelfServicePurchase on M365 License Manager, whose token
# audience is its application ID, so the scope must be set.
locals {
  self_service_purchase = {
    CFQ7TTC0MM8R = "Disabled" # Microsoft 365 Copilot
    CFQ7TTC0LH3L = "Disabled" # Power Automate per user
  }
}

resource "msrest_update_resource" "self_service_purchase" {
  for_each = local.self_service_purchase

  url           = "https://licensing.m365.microsoft.com/v1/policies/AllowSelfServicePurchase/products/${each.key}"
  scope         = "aeb86249-8ea3-49e2-900b-54cc8e308f85/.default"
  update_method = "PUT"
  body          = { policyValue = each.value }

  # The licensing API answers parallel writes with HTTP 412, so write the
  # products one at a time.
  concurrency = "m365-licensing"

  # Optional: restore the default when the resource is destroyed.
  delete_method = "PUT"
  delete_body   = { policyValue = "Enabled" }

  response_export_values = { product_name = "productName" }
}

output "copilot_product_name" {
  value = msrest_update_resource.self_service_purchase["CFQ7TTC0MM8R"].output.product_name
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `body` (Dynamic) The properties to set, as an HCL object such as `{ allowCalendarSharing = false }`. It is sent as JSON. Only these properties are compared on refresh. A property the API does not return is treated as write-only and never shows drift.
- `url` (String) Absolute URL the object is written to (and read from, unless `read_url` is set). Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `concurrency` (String) Name of a concurrency group: resources in the same group write one at a time, for APIs that reject parallel writes (the self-service purchase policies of the licensing API answer them with HTTP 412). The group covers the write, the reads after it until the values show up (`read_after_write_timeout`), and the request of `delete_method`. Reads on refresh are not serialized. The group holds within one provider process, that is, one provider configuration of one run; for writes from elsewhere, a 412 without a client precondition (`If-Match`, `If-None-Match`, `If-Unmodified-Since`) is retried. Changing it writes nothing.
- `delete_body` (Dynamic) HCL object sent as JSON with `delete_method`, for example to restore defaults. Without it, the destroy request has no body.
- `delete_method` (String) HTTP method sent to `url` on destroy: `DELETE`, `PATCH`, `PUT` or `POST`. When unset, destroying only removes the resource from the state and leaves the object as it is.
- `headers` (Map of String) Additional request headers, sent with every request (for example `OData-Version`).
- `read_after_write_timeout` (Number) Seconds to keep reading after a write until the API returns the written values (these APIs are eventually consistent). Defaults to `120`; `0` reads once without waiting. If the values do not show up in time, the apply still succeeds with a warning.
- `read_url` (String) Absolute URL to read the object from, if it differs from `url`.
- `response_export_values` (Map of String) Values of the response to export to `output`: the key is the name in `output`, the value a [JMESPath](https://jmespath.org/) query, `@` for the whole response. For example `{ all = "@", sharing = "allowCalendarSharing" }`.
- `scope` (String) OAuth scope (or resource) of the token, for example `https://tasks.office.com/.default` or `aeb86249-8ea3-49e2-900b-54cc8e308f85/.default`. Defaults to `https://<host of the request URL>/.default`.
- `update_method` (String) HTTP method that writes `body` on create and update: `PATCH` (default), `PUT` or `POST`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The `url` of the object.
- `output` (Dynamic) The values selected by `response_export_values` from the last read, as an HCL object (for example `msrest_update_resource.x.output.all`). An empty object when `response_export_values` is not set.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the URL of the object. The first plan after the import
# writes body once.
terraform import msrest_update_resource.planner https://tasks.office.com/taskAPI/tenantAdminSettings/Settings
```
